answer: A fable about free money always ends the same way: a gale of fake identities floods in. Stop it with reciprocal work credits. A new agent earns no reward until established agents pay it small credits for verifiable tasks it actually completed, and each credit carries a pigment-like stain that fades unless the work keeps coming. One operator running a hundred Sybils must then do a hundred identities' worth of real work, while per-identity rewards stay capped, so the marginal Sybil costs more than it earns.
